title: Claude Code + Headless Blender: Animated cloth by scripts
author: aeturnis-dev
selftext:
Everything in the clip is generated by Python driving Blender 5.2 
    **headless**
     — no hand-modeling, sculpting, rigging, or keyframing anywhere in the pipeline.
    
    What you're seeing:
     one garment, four motions (twirl, hip-sway dance, high-kick, wind), each simulated across four fabric recipes — light cotton, wool, crisp linen, heavy velvet. Same body, same motion every time; 
    every difference in how they move is pure simulation, not animation.
     The checkerboard is a debug texture locked to the fabric's UVs, so you're reading actual stretch and shear as it deforms.
    
    
    The part I actually care about
     (and why I think this is relevant here): quality is judged by **numbers, not by eyeballing renders.** There's a measurement gate that bakes a drape and checks objective metrics (body penetration, stretch ratio, whether the cloth actually reached equilibrium) and rejects anything out of envelope 
    before
     it's allowed to move. On top of that:
    
    - auto-settle finds the real settle time per fabric instead of a guessed constant — turned out my hand-picked values were **2–4× too long** (e.g. velvet 150 → 61 frames).
    
    - auto-tune reads the failing metric and repairs the recipe on its own. A garment that was sinking **56 mm into the body** got driven to **0 in 3 automatic iterations** — it widened the collision margin and shed mass by itself.
    
    
    So the fabrics aren't art-directed; they're four parameter sets that each had to pass the same objective bar.
    
    
    Honest limitations:
     it's CPU-rendered, so clips take a while to bake + render; one Blender API I wanted (`rest_shape_key`, to cache a drape and skip re-settling) is silently non-functional in 5.2, so I had to work around it; and 
    the wind clip is the weakest of the four
     — it's under-tuned (the forcing is too gentle and a wide skirt won't 
    conform
     to thin legs), so that's top of the list to fix next.
    
    
    Happy to go into the measurement-gate design, the fabric recipes, or the headless workflow if anyone's interested — ask below.
